newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal juggles rules for supermarket sites.
newsitem.headline: Portugal juggles rules for supermarket sites.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government on Wednesday made a slight change to the rules covering the location of hypermarkets that local companies said would favour foreign competitors seeking to enter the market.
The cabinet decided that permission for licences would no longer be based solely the size of the proposed site, but on the overall volume of sales by the group seeking to open the new store.
The Portuguese Association of Retailers (APED) said the decision would contribute to the "stagnation of the sector."

"At a moment in which commercial companies need to grow rapidly to gain critical mass and competitive capacity, the new law...will make it more difficult for national groups to grow and facilitate the entry of new foreign groups," it said.
Under pressure from small shop owners, the government last year forced hypermarkets to limit the number of hours they opened on Sundays and public holidays.
